_doc: Words no ad the studio offers should carry by default. ONE list, read by scripts/ad_census.mjs (DESIGN-LAW 143): every word on every offered ad, as a visitor opens it, is matched against it, and --gate fails an ad that carries one. Started 2026-11-18 from docs/COMPETITOR-RESEARCH-2026-11-12.md section 5.2 ('What to leave out'), with the house's own lists that say the same thing beside it: the full ad's pre-flight (motion/fullad.js fullWords, PROOF: rule 138), rule 55 (no dollar figure, no invented proof, no deadline, no dash in customer copy) and rule 136 (a phone ad asks for a text, not a picture). Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions, matched case-insensitively on the ad's words with accents kept (the census upper-cases them first). 'unless': the entry is not matched when this pattern is also in the same line (a limit given). 'only': the entry applies to ads of these categories alone. To add a phrase, add a row; to retire one, delete it. A customer's own typed words are theirs: the census types only a number, a website, a business name and an area, so every other word it finds is the studio's.

phrases.label: UP TO $
phrases.why: Read as the typical price and flagged by regulators; the pre-flight says it too.

phrases.label: TOP DOLLAR
phrases.why: The most generic phrase in the category: on sign-shop posters and the franchise's captions, so it says nothing about who is buying.

phrases.label: HIGHEST
phrases.why: A comparative claim that may need proof.

phrases.label: BEST PRICE
phrases.why: A comparative claim that may need proof.

phrases.label: WE BEAT ANY OFFER
phrases.why: A comparative claim that may need proof.

phrases.label: ANY CONDITION (no limit)
phrases.why: With no limit it reads as no questions asked.

phrases.label: ICLOUD LOCKED / OK
phrases.why: Reads as no questions asked; the category has a documented stolen-goods problem.

phrases.label: TODAY ONLY
phrases.why: The FTC's named pressure signal; rule 55 allows urgency only when it is true.

phrases.label: BEST
phrases.why: A claim that needs proof (BEST PRICE is its own row).

phrases.label: a dollar figure
phrases.why: Prices move and a picture does not: no dollar figure on a graphic by default (an owner-entered, dated price line is the research's own proposal, 5.1 no. 3). An UP TO price is its own row.

phrases.label: an en or em dash
phrases.why: No em or en dash in anything a customer reads.

phrases.label: TEXT A PIC (phone ads)
phrases.why: A phone ad asks for a text (the IMEI), not a picture: the buyer's chatbot quotes from what is typed.
